title: A button press turns the light on, and the relay confirms it
description: Drive the Toggle's digital input high; the press propagates over the IToggler → IToggleable contract and the Light switches on, counting the switch-on and accumulating on-time on its 1 s timer. The light's digital output is paired with the IdealRelay's provider face in the topology, so the command it writes actually arrives somewhere: the relay receives it, confirms the value it applied, and that confirmation comes back on the light's OutputChanged as ConfirmedOn — the far side a workstation otherwise does not have. Pressing again switches the loop back off. Deterministic under `dale dev --stepped`.

steps.label: Press the button (digital input goes high)
Hold it on for 3 s of virtual time
…and its digital output mirrors the On state
The pairing delivered that command to the relay's provider face
…and the relay's confirmation came back on OutputChanged
Release the button (a release does not toggle in this mode)
…and the loop settles: the relay confirms the lamp went out too
…on a second command, not a repeat of the first

judge.text: TotalTimeOn is about 3 s after the hold (the [Timer(1)] accumulates only while the light is on)
ConfirmedOn tracks On rather than leading it — the block's own state changes first, the confirmation follows a round trip later
